title: What If Every Human Vanished Overnight?

scenes.text: What if every human vanished tonight? The first disaster wouldn't take long to arrive.
Within about thirty-six hours, with the pumps off, engineers say the New York subway tunnels would flood completely.
Unwatched nuclear plants and oil facilities could fail, causing fires and radiation releases. The author of The World Without Us calls that the wildcard.
After a few years, winter cracks the pavement, seeds take root, and water corrodes the metal beneath the streets.
Within about five hundred years, many cities would be forest. The plastic would still be here after thousands.
Extra carbon dioxide could take up to a hundred thousand years to clear. We'd be gone, but our air wouldn't.

description:
What if every human vanished overnight?
Subways flood within about a day and a half, cities turn to forest in about five hundred years, and our carbon dioxide lingers for thousands.
What should we run through next?
